habitat: Moist evergreen forests of peninsular India and Northeast India
ecological_importance: Provides nesting and roosting sites for canopy birds. Flowers offer abundant nectar for bees and bats. Ripe fruits are eaten by civets, bats, and monkeys.
field_identification_notes: Unmistakable bipinnate leaves with wedge-shaped, fishtail-like leaflets.
Ringed trunk with prominent leaf scar bands.
Cascading, rope-like flower clusters hanging from the upper stem nodes.
ml_relevance: Bipinnate fronds with jagged, wedge-shaped 'fishtail' leaflets provide a unique high-confidence visual signature for computer vision models.

ar_information.quick_identification: Bipinnate fronds with jagged, fishtail-shaped leaflets; ringed grey trunk.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Supports nectar-feeding insects and arboreal frugivores.
ar_information.conservation_message: Least Concern (LC). This palm is monocarpic-it flowers sequentially from top to bottom over several years before dying.

vit_campus_relevance.location: Campus botanical gardens and landscaping zones
